name: Sikafloor-169

SIKAFLOOR®-169: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-169, April 2023, Version 04.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sikafloor_-169.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-169 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 04.01).
1.2 Product description. Sikafloor®-169 is a two part, very low yellowing, low viscous, transparent epoxy resin.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikafloor®-169 may only be used by experienced professionals. Sikafloor®-169 is used as:
    - Transparent binder for coloured quartz mortars and screeds like Sikafloor® Decodur ES-22 Granite, Sikafloor® Decodur ES-26 Flake, Sikafloor® Decodur EB- 26 Quartz and Sikafloor® Decodur EM-21 Compact
    - Transparent sealer coat for broadcast colour quartz mortar screeds and smooth coatings fully broadcast to excess with coloured chips
    - Suitable for normal up to medium heavy and heavy mechanical loading
    - Particularly used in the food and pharmaceutical industries, for show rooms, workshops and production areas etc.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.11.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-169
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Sikafloor®-169 is a two part, very low yellowing, transparent epoxy resin.
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability. Sikafloor®-169 conforms to the requirements of LEED EQ Credit 4.2: Low-Emitting Materials: Paints & Coatings EPA Reference Test Method 24 VOC Content < 100 g/l
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - Biological resistance certificate Sikafloor®-169 CSM Statement of Qualification – ISO 846, very good - Report No. SI 1008-533.
    - Food compliance according to EC Nr. 1935/2004 and the German Food and Feed Act, Hygiene Institut des Ruhrgebiet; test report H-193755-10 August 2010 ( tested system: Sikafloor® -169 sealed with Sikafloor®-304 W )
    - Eurofins Emission testing of Sikafloor®-169 according to the AgBB-scheme and guidelines of the DiBt (AgBB – Committee for Health-related Evaluation of Building Products, DiBt – German Institute for Building Technology).
    - Sampling, testing and evaluation were performed according to ISO-16000, Report No. 766563C.
    - Synthetic resin screed material according to EN 13813:2002, Declaration of Performance 02 08 01 02 009 0000010 1008, certified by notified factory production control certification body 0921, certificate of conformity of the factory production control 2017, and provided with the CE marking.
    - Coating for surface protection of concrete according to EN 1504-2:2004, Declaration of Performance 02 08 01 02 009 0000010 1008, certified by notified factory production control certification body 0921, certificate of conformity of the factory production control 2017, and provided with the CE marking.
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ISO 846: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 13813:2002: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1504-2:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - DIN 53 505: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Abrasion resistance (p.2); Technical Information > Shore D Hardness (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Transparent
    - Low VOC-content
    - Low yellowing
    - Good mechanical and abrasion resistance
    - Low viscous
    - Easy application
    - Multi-purpose binder
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy
2.7 Appearance and colour.
    | Resin - part A: | turbid, liquid |
    | Hardener - part B: | yellowish, liquid |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.8 Density.
    | Part A | ~ 1.1 kg/l |
    | Part B | ~ 1.0 kg/l |
    | Mixed resin | ~ 1.1 kg/l |
    | All Density values at +23°C. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
2.9 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore D Hardness: ~80 (7 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Abrasion resistance: 47 mg (CS 10/1000/1000) (8 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Chemical resistance: Resistant to many chemicals. Contact Sika technical service for specific information.
2.10 Temperature resistance.
    | Exposure* | Dry heat |
    | Permanent | +50 °C |
    | Short-term max. 7 d | +80 °C |
    | Short-term max. 12 h | +100 °C |
    Short-term moist/wet heat* up to +80 °C where exposure is only occasional (steam cleaning etc.).
    Note printed: *No simultaneous chemical and mechanical exposure and only in combination with Sikafloor® systems as a broadcast system with approx. 3 - 4 mm thickness.
2.11 Systems. Please refer to the system data sheet of :
    | Sikafloor® Decodur ES-22 Granite | Smooth low voc coloured granite ef- |
    | fect epoxy floor covering |
    | Sikafloor® Decodur ES-26 Flake | Smooth low voc coloured full flaked |
    | epoxy floor covering |
    | Sikafloor® Decodur EB-26 Quartz | Slip resistant low voc colour quartz |
    | broadcasted epoxy floor covering |
    | Sikafloor® Decodur EM-21 Compact | Smooth high resistant power floated |
    | broadcast colour quartz epoxy screed |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.12 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.
2.13 Packaging.
    | Part A: | 6kg containers |
    | Part B: | 2 kg containers |
    | Part A+B: | 8 kg unipacks |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 04.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - The concrete substrate must be sound and of sufficient compressive strength (minimum 25 N/mm²) with a minimum pull off strength of 1.5 N/mm².
    - The substrate must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc.
    - High spots must be removed by e.g. grinding.
    - All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by brush and/or vacuum.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 04.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : part B = 75 : 25 (by weight)
4.3 Consumption. ~0.15 - 0.3 kg/m² applied as sealing coats; ~0.7-2 kg/m² applied as a wearing course; These figures are theoretical and do not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level or wastage etc. For detailed info, please refer to the System data sheet Sikafloor® Decodur ES-22 granite, Sikafloor® Decodur ES-26 flake, Sikafloor® Decodur EB-26 Quartz and Sikafloor® Decodur EM-21 Compact.
4.4 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Time |
    | +10 °C | ~ 60 minutes |
    | +20 °C | ~ 30 minutes |
    | +30 °C | ~ 20 minutes |
4.5 Curing time. Before overcoating Sikafloor®-169 allow:
    | Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum |
    | +10°C | 45 hours | 4 days |
    | +20°C | 36 hours | 3 days |
    | +30°C | 24 hours | 2 days |
    Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.
4.6 Applied product ready for use.
    | Temperature | Foot traffic | Light traffic | Full cure |
    | +10 °C | ~ 36 hours | ~ 5 days | ~ 10 days |
    | +20 °C | ~ 12 hours | ~ 3 days | ~ 7 days |
    | +30 °C | ~ 8 hours | ~ 2 days | ~ 5 days |
    Note: Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions.
4.7 Mixing.
    - Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A, mix continuously for 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved.
    - To ensure thorough mixing pour materials into another container and mix again to achieve a consistent mix. Over mixing must be avoided to minimise air entrainment.
    - When using an additional C component like the Sikafloor®-CompactFiller or the Sikafloor®-DecoFiller, please add the C component after Parts A and B have been mixed, in the correct mixing ratio (Slurry Sika-CompactFloor; 1 part resin: 1 part Sikafloor®-CompactFiller; Wearing course Sika-DecoFloor; 1 part resin: 1,5 part Sikafloor®-DecoFiller) and mix for a further 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved.
    - For mortars add the premixed Sikafloor®-169 to the aggregates and mix until a uniform mix has been achieved.
4.8 Mixing - Mixing Tools.
    - Sikafloor®-169 must be thoroughly mixed using a low speed electric stirrer
    - (300 - 400 rpm) or other suitable equipment.
    - For the preparation of mortars use a forced action mixer of rotating pan, paddle or trough type. Free fall mixers must not be used.
4.9 Application. Please refer to the System data sheet Sikafloor® Decodur ES-22 granite, Sikafloor® Decodur ES-26 flake, Sikafloor® Decodur EB-26 Quartz and Sikafloor® Decodur EM-21 Compact.
4.10 Cleaning of equipment.
    - Clean all tools and application equipment with Thinner C immediately after use.
    - Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically
4.11 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-169 on substrates with rising moisture.
    - Freshly applied Sikafloor®-169 should be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 24 hours.
    - Trials should be carried out on mortar mixes to confirm and evaluate suitable aggregate colour blends and size distribution (granulometry).
    - The incorrect assessment and treatment of cracks may lead to a reduced service life and reflective cracking.
    - Under certain conditions, under floor heating or high ambient temperatures combined with high point loading, may lead to imprints in the resin.
    - Under UV-exposure some discolouration (yellowing) will occur, however this has no influence on the function and performance of the coating.
    - If heating is required do not use gas, oil, paraffin or other fossil fuel heaters, these produce large quantities of both CO2 and H2O water vapour, which may adversely affect the finish. For heating use only electric powered warm air blower systems.
4.12 Further information.
    - Substrate quality & Preparation
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “EVALUATION AND PREPARATION OF SURFACES FOR FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
    - Application instructions
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “MIXING & APPLICATION OF FLOORING SYSTEMS”. Maintenance
    - Please refer to “Sikafloor®- CLEANING REGIME”.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 80 % r.h. max.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish. Note: Low temperatures and high humidity conditions increase the probability of blooming.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. < 4 % pbw moisture content. Test method: Sika®-Tramex meter, CM-measurement or Oven-dry-method. No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.11):
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-169 on substrates with rising moisture.
    - Under certain conditions, under floor heating or high ambient temperatures combined with high point loading, may lead to imprints in the resin.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Part A | ~ 1.1 kg/l; Part B | ~ 1.0 kg/l; Mixed resin | ~ 1.1 kg/l; All Density values at +23°C. (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Shore D Hardness: ~80 (7 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Abrasion resistance: 47 mg (CS 10/1000/1000) (8 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-169, April 2023, Version 04.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sikafloor_-169.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-169 Part B, version 18/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sds-sikafloor-169partb.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-169 Part A, version 05/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/sds-sikafloor-169parta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For infromation and advice on safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
6.4 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
